title: Kestrel and the Bell
premise: Cyrus Marchetti, a reclusive urban explorer who documents unmapped tunnels beneath his inherited house, notices the mirrors lagging one second behind reality—and in that stolen second, something else moves. The house was built by his grandfather over a flooded bell foundry where, in 1974, six workers vanished and a bronze bell was pried from the drowned shaft and hidden in the walls. As frost spreads inward through every mirror and window, Cyrus learns his family's silence bought them safety while the trapped workers' echoes paid the price. To end it, he must descend, return the bell to the water, and speak the names no one would say—accepting that truth will cost him the belonging he's spent his life avoiding.
about_author: Noor Ishikawa is a former building surveyor who spent a decade inspecting basements and sub-basements across rust-belt cities before turning to horror fiction. They write about architecture as memory, and live above a decommissioned foundry they refuse to enter after dark.

chapters.title: The Second Behind the Glass
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Mapping the tunnels beneath his late grandfather's house, Cyrus logs an unmapped brick corridor, then notices his bathroom mirror reflecting him a beat too slow. He tells himself it's fatigue. Emotional beat: unease disguised as routine—the moment control begins slipping.

chapters.title: Doors Counted Twice
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. His compulsive rituals—counting doors, checking locks—start failing because rooms rearrange between counts. He finds a 1974 newspaper clipping about six missing foundry workers sealed inside a wall cavity. Emotional beat: dread deepens as his systems of safety turn against him.

chapters.title: What Grandfather Kept
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus, with flashbacks in his grandfather Aldo's voice via journal entries. The journals admit the family hid 'the bell' after the flood collapse, and that 'the quiet holds if you never look.' Emotional beat: betrayal—loyalty to family revealed as complicity in a cover-up.

chapters.title: Frost on the Inside
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Frost blooms on interior windows and mirrors despite summer heat; each pane shows the drowned foundry shaft instead of the room. A neighbor, Ruth Okafor, recognizes the pattern from her father's disappearance in '74. Emotional beat: isolation cracks—an ally appears.

chapters.title: Six Names
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Cyrus and Ruth. In city archives they recover the workers' names, all misfiled as 'structural loss.' The tunnel map Cyrus drew matches the foundry's original blueprints exactly—his exploration wasn't chance. Emotional beat: purpose forms from grief; loyalty to truth outweighs family silence.

chapters.title: The Corridor That Wasn't Surveyed
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Descending alone at night, Cyrus follows his own map into a corridor that extends past its drawn endpoint, walls sweating cold. Echoes of hammering answer his footsteps. He finds the bell behind a false wall, wrapped in tarp and chain. Emotional beat: awe curdling into terror—he was led here.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Touching the bell, Cyrus experiences the lag firsthand: he lives each moment once in the world and once in the mirror-world, where the six workers still walk their last shift. The frost reaches the ground floor. Emotional beat: confrontation with what staying invisible has cost everyone.

chapters.title: The Weight of Bronze
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus and Ruth. They rig ropes to haul the bell up the flooded shaft, but the house resists—doors seal, stairs lengthen, and the mirror-Cyrus argues he should stay and keep the family's bargain. Emotional beat: climax of internal conflict; loyalty to the dead versus loyalty to a corrupt inheritance.

chapters.title: Return to Water
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. At the shaft's edge, Cyrus speaks the six names aloud and lowers the bell into the black water. The mirror-world releases its hold—but the reflection keeps descending without him, taking the version of himself that hid. Emotional beat: sacrifice and release; truth spoken cannot be unspoken.

chapters.title: After the Frost
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus, epilogue-adjacent. Spring. The mirrors are only mirrors; the tunnels appear on a new municipal survey at last, and the six names go on a memorial plaque Ruth fought for. Cyrus still counts the doors—not from fear now, but as remembrance. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; belonging earned through truth rather than silence.
